Messages.Author: Orpheus
Messages.Body:
3.1.4. Withdrawing from an Event
Players choosing to withdraw from an event must inform the scorekeeper
before the seatings for the next round are generated. Players leaving the
tournament after the scorekeeper begins seatings for the next round receive
a "Loss" in the upcoming round and will be removed from the event after that
round.

And that is all. When a player withdraws from a table (yesterday we had one,
due to an urgent phone call), what does his predator gain in VPs and pool ?

--------

Orpheus

Messages.Body:

The judge ensures that the table balance is not unduly affected, and play

like, if the guy that just left was just about to be ousted anyway,
you'd probably give the predator 1 vp and 5 or 6 pool.

If it was, say, turn 2 of the game, you might just give nothing to the
predator.

if he was really strong and looking to hammer his prey soon, and in no
danger of being ousted by his predator at all you might give the
predator 0 vps, and give the prey a small penalty, perhaps.

basically, the judge uses his judgement to decide what 'adjustment'
needs to be made to make it as fair as possible.

Early departure is a big problem: normally I don't tolerate it (and if
someone leave the tournment without a good reason he lose all rights
to receive a prize).

The predator doesn't gain anything from the early departure of his
prey. The player who leave the game without announcing it before the
seating order is estabilished lose all rights on prizes and that's
all.

We have had such problem also during the EC in Barcelona and those are
the examples and I hope to remember correctly what the Barcelona EC
judges (and I was one of them with LSJ and Damnans) have decided for 2
problems similar to early departure:

PROBLEM 1
2 players are very late in a table of 5.
To keep the balance, if the table is reduced under the 4 players the
"table winner" (if one comes out) gains as much points as he has
partecipated to a table of 4.
There are only 3 players (A,B,C). A make a points and then C oust A. A
gets 1 point, B 0 points, C gets 3 points and a GW (instead of 2 and a
GW).
I don't remember because the problem was solved before the deadline
for the beginning of the round (the players arrived).

PROBLEM 2
A player leave a games because he want to concede (he has no vamp at
all and very small pool).

To keep the balance a judge will mantain a count of how much pool the
leaving player has. His predator has only to bleed 'till he kills his
prey then he get the point and 6 pools.

Best deranges to all who read!

RavATwoFaces

You have asked examples... I've given you 2.

As I've said you can't cover all the aspects for a "withdrawing from
an event"
Or you have to add a billion pages to the rule.

It's up to the judge giving a solution to that problem... and he must
consider a lot of factors... but the predator NORMALLY will not gain
points for a player who leave the game in the middle.

Cancelling him from the seating order normally is a good solution: the
judge can't make decisions on "guessing" like:
if he stay here 2 more turns I oust him...
he can't go backwards but he can make a lot of pressure to his prey...

OK! It's not the BEST solution but, for what I know, it's the only
good solution...

Oh! If the withdrawing happened in the first 10-15 minutes of a game,
for me it's possible to begin the game again without that player
(adding 15 minutes to the time limit of that table).... but only if no
points are already scored.

RavATwoFaces
